kro: a ResourceGraphDefinition, Graph, GraphRevision, or an instance of an
RGD-generated kind. Conditions are reported in the object's status.conditions
list, which holds at most one entry per Type.

| `lastTransitionTime` _[Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#time-v1-meta)_ | Last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |

#### ConditionType

_Underlying type:_ _string_

ConditionType is the type of a status condition reported on kro resources.

ConditionType is an open string type, not a schema-validated enum: the API
server accepts any value in a condition's type field. The constants in this
package are the condition types kro itself sets on ResourceGraphDefinitions,
Graphs, and RGD-generated instances, so the same value (for example "Ready")
can appear for more than one resource kind. Other controllers or future kro
versions may report additional condition types.



_Appears in:_
- [Condition](#condition)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GraphAccepted` | RGDConditionTypeGraphAccepted is true when the RGD spec (schema and<br />resource templates) passes validation. False with reason<br />"InvalidResourceGraph" when the spec contains errors.<br /> |
| `GraphRevisionsResolved` | RGDConditionTypeGraphRevisionsResolved is true when all<br />GraphRevisions for this RGD have been discovered, no terminating<br />revisions remain in flight, and the latest revision's state in the<br />in-memory registry is known. Unknown while revisions are settling<br />(terminating GRs still deleting), warming (latest not yet in the<br />cache or registry), or compiling (latest is Pending). False when<br />the latest revision fails compilation.<br /> |
| `KindReady` | RGDConditionTypeKindReady is true when the generated<br />CustomResourceDefinition has been applied and its Established<br />condition is true.<br /> |
| `ControllerReady` | RGDConditionTypeControllerReady is true when the instance reconciler<br />for this RGD's generated kind is registered with the dynamic<br />controller and ready to reconcile instances.<br /> |
| `Ready` | InstanceConditionTypeReady is the root condition on an instance of an<br />RGD-generated kind. It is true only when InstanceManaged, GraphResolved,<br />and ResourcesReady are all true for the current generation; otherwise<br />it mirrors the status, reason, and message of the least healthy of them.<br /> |
| `InstanceManaged` | InstanceConditionTypeInstanceManaged is true when kro has set the<br />finalizers and labels it needs to manage the instance. False with<br />reason "ManagementFailed" otherwise.<br /> |
| `GraphResolved` | InstanceConditionTypeGraphResolved is true when the instance's runtime<br />graph has been created and all of its resources resolved. False with<br />reason "ResolutionFailed" otherwise.<br /> |
| `ResourcesReady` | InstanceConditionTypeResourcesReady is true when every resource in the<br />instance's graph has been created and is ready. False with reason<br />"NotReady" while resources are still converging, or "ResourceDeleting"<br />while managed resources are terminating.<br /> |
| `Ready` | GraphConditionTypeReady is true when the graph has converged on its<br />desired state: every node has been reconciled and reports ready.<br /> |
| `Accepted` | GraphConditionTypeAccepted is true when the graph spec passes<br />validation (unique node IDs, well-formed expressions, dependency<br />graph is acyclic). False with reason "InvalidGraph" otherwise.<br /> |

#### Contribution



Contribution is a lightweight record of a patch node's field-manager
contribution to a resource this Graph does not own. It mirrors the
in-memory executor contribution: the tuple identifies the target
(APIVersion, Kind, Namespace, Name, Subresource) and FieldManager is the
dedicated server-side-apply manager the contributed fields were applied
under. On prune/teardown the manager relinquishes exactly those fields;
the target object is never deleted.



_Appears in:_
- [GraphStatus](#graphstatus)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiVersion` _string_ | APIVersion of the patched target ("apps/v1", "v1", ...). |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `kind` _string_ | Kind of the patched target ("Deployment", "ConfigMap", ...). |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `namespace` _string_ | Namespace of the patched target. Empty for cluster-scoped targets. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |
| `name` _string_ | Name of the patched target. |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `subresource` _string_ | Subresource the contribution was applied through ("status" for a<br />status patch, empty for the main resource). |  | Optional: {} <br /> |
| `fieldManager` _string_ | FieldManager is the dedicated server-side-apply field manager the<br />contributed fields were applied under. Release relinquishes the fields<br />owned by this manager on the target. |  | Required: {} <br /> |

#### ForEachDimension

_Underlying type:_ _object_

ForEachDimension defines a single expansion axis in a forEach block.
Each dimension is a map with exactly one entry where the key is the variable name
and the value is the CEL expression. Example: {"region": "${schema.spec.regions}"}
Multiple dimensions create a cartesian product of expansions.

_Validation:_
- MaxProperties: 1
- MinProperties: 1

_Appears in:_
- [Node](#node)
- [Resource](#resource)

#### ManagedResource



ManagedResource is a lightweight pointer to a cluster resource the Graph
controller has applied. The tuple of (APIVersion, Kind, Namespace, Name)
identifies the resource; UID is captured post-apply for safe deletion
(preconditioned on UID so we never delete an impostor recreated by some
other actor between apply and prune).



_Appears in:_
- [GraphStatus](#graphstatus)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeID` _string_ | NodeID is the Graph node that produced this resource. Multiple<br />resources may share a NodeID for forEach expansions. |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `apiVersion` _string_ | APIVersion of the resource ("apps/v1", "v1", ...). |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `kind` _string_ | Kind of the resource ("Deployment", "ConfigMap", ...). |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `namespace` _string_ | Namespace of the resource. Empty for cluster-scoped resources. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |
| `name` _string_ | Name of the resource. |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `uid` _string_ | UID returned by the API server when the resource was applied. Used<br />as a delete precondition so we don't remove a resource that was<br />deleted-and-recreated out of band between apply and prune.<br />A UID-less entry is a not-yet-observed intent (e.g. a pre-apply<br />write-ahead entry declared but not yet applied this cycle). Such an<br />entry is intentionally SKIPPED on delete/prune: without a captured UID<br />kro cannot prove the live object is the one it applied, and deleting by<br />name alone could remove an object kro does not own. It is therefore<br />effectively required for cleanup — an entry only becomes deletable once<br />a successful apply has recorded its UID. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |

which determines its behavior. Node IDs are the handles other nodes use to
reference it via CEL expressions.

Each resource can either be created using a template or reference an existing resource.
Resources can depend on each other through CEL expressions, creating a dependency graph.

#### ResourceGraphDefinition



ResourceGraphDefinition is the core API for defining reusable groups of Kubernetes resources.
It allows you to create custom resources that manage multiple underlying resources as a cohesive unit.
When you create a ResourceGraphDefinition, kro automatically generates a CRD and deploys a controller
to manage instances of your custom resource. Resources can reference each other using CEL expressions,
and kro ensures they are created in the correct dependency order.





| Field | Description | Default | Validation |

| `apiVersion` _string_ | `kro.run/v1alpha1` | | |

#### ResourceGraphDefinitionSpec



ResourceGraphDefinitionSpec defines the desired state of ResourceGraphDefinition.
It contains the schema for instances (defining the CRD structure) and the list of
Kubernetes resources that make up the graph.



_Appears in:_
- [ResourceGraphDefinition](#resourcegraphdefinition)
- [ResourceGraphDefinitionSnapshot](#resourcegraphdefinitionsnapshot)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` _[Schema](#schema)_ | Schema defines the structure of instances created from this ResourceGraphDefinition.<br />It specifies the API version, kind, and fields (spec/status) for the generated CRD.<br />Use SimpleSchema syntax to define the instance schema concisely. |  | Required: {} <br /> |
| `resources` _[Resource](#resource) array_ | Resources is the list of Kubernetes resources that will be created and managed<br />for each instance. Resources can reference each other using CEL expressions,<br />creating a dependency graph that determines creation order. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |


#### ResourceGraphDefinitionState

_Underlying type:_ _string_

ResourceGraphDefinitionState defines the state of the resource graph definition.



_Appears in:_
- [ResourceGraphDefinitionStatus](#resourcegraphdefinitionstatus)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | ResourceGraphDefinitionStateActive represents the active state of the resource definition.<br /> |
| `Inactive` | ResourceGraphDefinitionStateInactive represents the inactive state of the resource graph definition<br /> |


#### ResourceGraphDefinitionStatus



ResourceGraphDefinitionStatus defines the observed state of ResourceGraphDefinition.
It provides information about the deployment state, resource ordering, and conditions.



_Appears in:_
- [ResourceGraphDefinition](#resourcegraphdefinition)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` _[ResourceGraphDefinitionState](#resourcegraphdefinitionstate)_ | State indicates whether the ResourceGraphDefinition is Active or Inactive.<br />Active means the graph is accepted and the generated CRD and dynamic controller<br />are currently serving.<br />Inactive means the current graph is not accepted or the RGD is not currently serving. |  |  |
| `topologicalOrder` _string array_ | TopologicalOrder is the ordered list of resource IDs based on their dependencies.<br />Resources are created in this order to ensure dependencies are satisfied.<br />Example: ["configmap", "deployment", "service"] |  |  |
| `conditions` _[Conditions](#conditions)_ | Conditions represent the latest available observations of the ResourceGraphDefinition's state.<br />Common condition types include "Ready", "GraphRevisionsResolved", "GraphAccepted",<br />"KindReady", and "ControllerReady". |  |  |
| `resources` _[ResourceInformation](#resourceinformation) array_ | Resources provides detailed information about each resource in the graph,<br />including their dependencies. |  |  |
| `lastIssuedRevision` _integer_ | LastIssuedRevision is the highest GraphRevision revision number ever issued for this RGD.<br />It is a persisted high-water mark used to keep revision allocation monotonic across GC. |  |  |


#### ResourceInformation



ResourceInformation provides detailed information about a specific resource
in the ResourceGraphDefinition, particularly its dependencies on other resources.



_Appears in:_
- [GraphRevisionStatus](#graphrevisionstatus)
- [ResourceGraphDefinitionStatus](#resourcegraphdefinitionstatus)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` _string_ | ID is the unique identifier of the resource as defined in the resources list. |  |  |
| `dependencies` _[Dependency](#dependency) array_ | Dependencies lists all resources that this resource depends on.<br />A resource depends on another if it references it in a CEL expression.<br />These dependencies determine the order of resource creation. |  |  |


#### ResourceScope

_Underlying type:_ _string_

ResourceScope defines whether the generated instance CRD is Namespaced or Cluster scoped.

_Validation:_
- Enum: [Namespaced Cluster]

_Appears in:_
- [Schema](#schema)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Namespaced` | ResourceScopeNamespaced means the generated instance CRD will be namespace-scoped.<br />This is the default.<br /> |
| `Cluster` | ResourceScopeCluster means the generated instance CRD will be cluster-scoped.<br /> |


#### Schema



Schema defines the structure and behavior of instances created from a ResourceGraphDefinition.
It specifies the API group, version, and kind for the generated CRD, along with the
spec and status schemas using SimpleSchema syntax. You can also define custom types,
validation rules, and printer columns.



_Appears in:_
- [ResourceGraphDefinitionSpec](#resourcegraphdefinitionspec)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` _string_ | Kind is the name of the custom resource type that will be created.<br />This becomes the kind field of the generated CRD and must be a valid Kubernetes kind name<br />(PascalCase, starting with a capital letter). This field is immutable after creation.<br />Example: "WebApplication", "Database", "MicroService" |  | Pattern: `^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,62}$` <br />Required: {} <br /> |
| `plural` _string_ | Plural is the plural form of Kind used as the resource name in the generated<br />CRD, forming its name as "&lt;plural&gt;.&lt;group&gt;". If omitted, it is derived by<br />pluralizing the lowercased kind, which follows English rules and is not always<br />what you would expect or might even not be correct. (For example: "PodInfo" becomes "podinfoes").<br />Set this explicitly to override the generated value.<br />This field is immutable after creation! It cannot be changed again. |  | MaxLength: 63 <br />Optional: {} <br />Pattern: `^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$` <br /> |
| `apiVersion` _string_ | APIVersion is the version identifier for the generated CRD.<br />Must follow Kubernetes versioning conventions (v1, v1alpha1, v1beta1, etc.).<br />This field is immutable after creation.<br />Example: "v1alpha1", "v1", "v2beta1" |  | Pattern: `^v[0-9]+(alpha[0-9]+\|beta[0-9]+)?$` <br />Required: {} <br /> |
| `group` _string_ | Group is the API group for the generated CRD. Together with APIVersion and Kind,<br />it forms the complete GVK (Group-Version-Kind) identifier.<br />If omitted, defaults to "kro.run". This field is immutable after creation.<br />Example: "mycompany.io", "databases.example.com" | kro.run | Optional: {} <br /> |
| `spec` _[RawExtension](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#rawextension-runtime-pkg)_ | Spec defines the schema for the instance's spec section using SimpleSchema syntax.<br />This becomes the OpenAPI schema for instances of the generated CRD.<br />Use SimpleSchema's concise syntax to define fields, types, defaults, and validations.<br />Markers are space-separated after a single "\|" separator.<br />Example: {"replicas": "integer \| default=1 minimum=1 maximum=10"} |  |  |
| `types` _[RawExtension](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#rawextension-runtime-pkg)_ | Types is a map of custom type definitions that can be referenced in the Spec.<br />This allows you to define reusable complex types using SimpleSchema syntax.<br />Reference custom types in Spec using the type name.<br />Example: {"Server": {"host": "string", "port": "integer"}} |  |  |
| `status` _[RawExtension](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#rawextension-runtime-pkg)_ | Status defines the schema for the instance's status section using SimpleSchema syntax.<br />Unlike spec, status fields use CEL expressions to project values from underlying resources.<br />This allows you to surface important information from managed resources at the instance level.<br />Example: {"connectionName": "${database.status.connectionName}", "endpoint": "${service.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].hostname}"} |  |  |
| `scope` _[ResourceScope](#resourcescope)_ | Scope determines whether the generated instance CRD is Namespaced or Cluster scoped.<br />Defaults to Namespaced to preserve existing behaviour. This field is immutable after creation. | Namespaced | Enum: [Namespaced Cluster] <br />Required: {} <br /> |
| `additionalPrinterColumns` _[CustomResourceColumnDefinition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.36/#customresourcecolumndefinition-v1-apiextensions-k8s-io) array_ | AdditionalPrinterColumns defines additional printer columns<br />that will be passed down to the created CRD. If set, no<br />default printer columns will be added to the created CRD,<br />and if default printer columns need to be retained, they<br />need to be added explicitly. |  | Optional: {} <br /> |
